Agent swarms are going to be a core part of many enterprise workflows in the future. The ability to throw compute at problems that you can massively parallelize will be too useful to not take advantage of. 

Cyber will be one of the biggest beneficiaries of this as it’s a space where testing vast number of permutations of attacks (without getting tired or bored) is an incredibly useful property. You have a wide search space of possible risk vectors and you generally need to be able to chain together different scenarios to achieve the exploit. 

This will become one of the biggest token uses in large enterprises given the range of IT systems, software, physical infrastructure, and data that needs to be protected at all times. Super interesting times in cyber.

I just heard the most touching AI coding story.

A friend @vicyaqingyang grew up in a modest home full of cockroaches. To turn lemons into lemonade, her mom made killing them a game.

When she told this story to another friend, that friend vibe coded a game from it. You catch cockroaches in a room and compete against Mom.

She cried while playing it.

The game isn’t technically sophisticated. Any model can build it pretty quickly now. What gives it a soul is the human story, experience, and emotion behind it.

Code is the new medium for storytelling.

x.name: Qwen
x.bio: Open foundation models for AGI.

tweets.text: QwenGyre addresses two challenges of XLong-horizon agentic RL. https://t.co/v5sIbZmz0S

Introducing QwenGyre, bringing elastic RL to extreme-long-horizon (XLong) agent training. ✨

It launches with two core designs: 🥳
- Elastic Scheduler: reallocates GPUs between rollout & training as demand shifts—live executions never interrupted. Up to 1.85× speedup over Colocate, 1.78× over Async.
- Trajectory Processor: turns branching executions (compaction, sub-agents, retries) into prefix-shared trajectory trees with bounded, deduplicated training samples. Partial progress after timeout still gets scored.

Scaled to Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B with ~700K tokens per rollout, QwenGyre lifts NL2RepoBench from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps, cutting end-to-end training time by ~44% vs Async.

🔗 Read the paper:
https://t.co/gbKPIiqosk

tweets.text:
Because each sandbox holds a real checkout, agents search it with grep and standard file tools instead of relying on broad semantic searches.

On an internal benchmark of 150 financial-document questions, this reached 0.627 answer accuracy versus about 0.37 for semantic search. https://t.co/w1nmA0N8yz

A single long-lived sandbox per project would need provisioning for peak load and months of uptime.

Instead, repositories live on S3-backed storage and each agent runs in its own ephemeral sandbox, so a crash loses only unsubmitted work. https://t.co/dglC3ZI6AX

The CLI holds a short-lived lock to serialize submits, and the Git service accepts a submit only if it builds on the head, the latest accepted commit.

Otherwise, the agent replays its change on the new head and resubmits. https://t.co/urIrVVwPL7
